text:
pagerduty: PAGER: S1 alert — ingress ALB target groups in euc1b returning high 5xx rate (detected 10:34 UTC). paging sre-oncall :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: seeing a hard spike in 502/504s across the ALB backed by envoy. TCP resets on NLB backends too. routing graphs show weight shift to euc2 around the same time. starting mitigation checklist.

lara.m: confirmed customer-impacting — multiple EU customers reporting API errors. spike started ~10:33, sustained for ~6m. KD (key customers) affected: payment ingestion and webhooks.

aria.k: quick checks: ingress-controller pods show increasing accept queue and envoy downstream resets. healthchecks from ALB show OK for lb-target but app returning 5xx. possible conn reuse/keepalive/conntrack pressure?

mike.p: pulling logs now. seeing this pattern in envoy: 
```
[envoy] upstream connection reset while reading response
[envoy] code=502, upstream_reset_before_response_started
```

curl directly to node port returns 502 too.

mike.p: from host: `curl -sv https://api.internal.redwood/eval` output: 
```
* Received HTTP/2 stream 1 was reset: CANCEL
* Mark bundle as not supporting multiuse
* Connection #0 to host api.internal.redwood left intact
HTTP/2 502

{"error":"upstream reset"}
```

aria.k: also noticed a sudden route53 weighted policy drift — route weights for euc1b->euc2 changed ~10:32, likely due to automated failover from our routing policy. that amplified load cross-region.

sre-oncall: hypothesis: a combination of conntrack / keepalive exhaustion in euc1b ingress -> backends started returning resets -> routing policy moved weight -> traffic shear -> overload in euc2 and increased global 5xx. immediate mitigation plan: 1) pin route53 weights back to baseline, 2) scale ingress proxies in euc1b, 3) disable AWS ALB connection reuse via config if needed, 4) short-term rate-limit internal retries.

lara.m: agree. please coordinate with dns ops and infra. open an incident channel and post customer impact summary for support.

incidents-bot: Incident channel created: #incident-3812345678-ingress-euc1b. Summary: ALB/Envoy 5xx spike in euc1b, partial cross-region failover to euc2. Pages triggered.

aria.k: dns ops — can we push a weight rollback to restore normal traffic split?

mike.p: doing a route53 update now: 
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"euc1b","Weight":90,"TTL":10}}]}'
```

mike.p: submitted, propagation should be within the 10s TTL for our weighted policy. monitoring.

sre-oncall: scaling ingress controller in euc1b: 
```
kubectl --context=euc1b scale deployment ingress-proxy -n infra --replicas=6
```

deploy-bot: Scaling action recorded: ingress-proxy -> 6 replicas (euc1b).

mike.p: after route53 rollback and scale, 5xx rate dropped by ~60% within 45s. still seeing intermittent conn resets from a subset of nodes.

aria.k: let's check kernel conntrack and ephemeral port exhaustion on affected nodes. pulling node stats...

mike.p: sample output from node-12: 
```
# conntrack -S
nf_conntrack: used 120k, tcp 95k, max 128k
```

aria.k: used is close to max on some nodes. increasing conntrack or tuning keepalive should help. short-term: remove busiest nodes from ALB target group to drain.

sre-oncall: removing node-12 and node-13 from ALB target group (cordon+drain) to stop chaotic resets.

mike.p: ALB target deregister commands issued, draining traffic off nodes.

lara.m: customer comms — support drafted a banner and priority emails to affected accounts. ETA for full mitigation?

sre-oncall: mitigation effective, traffic stabilized, overall error rate back to baseline. ETA for full recovery: 30m while we observe.

pagerduty: NOTE: incident severity remains P1 until error rate steady for 30m.

aria.k: long-term items to add to follow-up: increase conntrack table size in AMI, tune kube-proxy conntrack settings, add ingress-proxy auto-scale policy for small spikes, and adjust routing policy to avoid aggressive weight shifts on transient signals.

mike.p: handoff incoming — I'm taking the incident for next shift. current state: traffic stable, nodes drained, route53 weight restored to 90/10, ingress scaled, conntrack on problematic nodes increased on a few hosts. continuing to monitor.

sre-oncall: handing off to mike.p for monitoring and RCA. all command history logged in incident channel. handoff checklist: confirm healthchecks stable, confirm no customer retries in backlog, ensure support has paused outbound comms until we have clean window.

mike.p: ack. will keep this thread updated every 10m and open a follow-up bug for the kernel tuning.

lara.m: excellent. please prep a short postmortem and include timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation, and action items. weave in any customer-impact timelines.

deploy-bot: Rolling back recent ingress-proxy config change suspected of reducing keepalive time: ingress-proxy-config v2026.03.10 -> v2026.03.09 rolled back (canary -> full).

mike.p: note: after rollback, we saw a further decrease in resets. putting as probable contributing factor.

incidents-bot: summary for RCA: Root cause candidate = aggressive routing weight shift + ingress keepalive/conntrack exhaustion + recent config change reducing keepalive. Impact: ~6m high-5xx window, partial customer failures for EU region. Current status: mitigated. Follow-ups assigned.

sre-oncall: closing live incident paging, keeping channel open for 1h for watch. will convert to postmortem after monitoring window if stable. :white_check_mark:

mike.p: confirmed stable at +28m. starting detailed timeline and creating ticket INF-4532 (conntrack tuning) and INF-4533 (routing policy backoff).

lara.m: thanks team. great coordination. schedule RCA within 72h and link to support contacts for customer follow-up.

aria.k: adding recommended ops playbook entry: on ingress 5xx with cross-region drift, prioritize routing weight rollback and target-group draining before global autoscaling adjustments.

pagerduty: INCIDENT: resolved (mitigated). Please ensure follow-up tasks are tracked and postmortem scheduled.

sre-oncall: final note: leave incident channel up and tag when postmortem ready. closing primary paging loop now.
